messages.subject: Pair error bars by group and factor
parts:
I want to create 10 separate plots for the example data. My aim is to create 2 plots for two consecutive pollutant pairs (identified by group) and listed in variable pollutant. For example I want to plot the effect of ozone and NO2 on outcome carvda together. Next the effect of ozone and nox on cardva etc..  In short I want to show the effect of two pollutants on outcome.

I have tried the following two codes, but none produced what I wanted.

 

Many thanks

  

 

ggplot(cv2, aes(x = pollutant, y = pinc, ymin = lcinc, ymax = ucinc)) +   

geom_pointrange(aes(col = factor(Outcome)) , position=position_dodge(width=0.8)) + ylab("Percent Increase in Mortality") +  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0))

 

 

ggplot(cv2, aes(x = Outcome, y = pinc, ymin = lcinc, ymax = ucinc)) +  geom_pointrange(aes(col = factor(pollutant)) , position=position_dodge(width=0.8)) + ylab("Percent Increase in Mortality") +

geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0))

 

dput(cv2)

structure(list(seq = 1:10, group = c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 2L,

1L, 2L, 1L, 2L), Outcome = c("cardva", "cardva", "cardva", "cardva",

"ami", "ami", "ami", "ami", "ischem", "ischem"), pinc = c(0.486650395378296,

0.177659502799266, 0.336008837290858, -0.0584360616549207, 1.63493735929263,

-0.0944930076043238, 1.56747902200582, -0.61520952974945, 1.38835268865829,

0.215263861567161), lcinc = c(-0.209746556913804, -0.346510459586569,

-0.336675159518951, -1.26213329261471, 0.225300283960195, -1.19039395153508,

0.122818263933677, -3.15119644128028, 0.191388311974583, -0.705470172350853

), ucinc = c(1.18790722825421, 0.704586560302722, 1.01323315783848,

1.15993524594977, 3.06440053321015, 1.01356261365932, 3.03298462585939,

1.98718222499203, 2.59961693425474, 1.14453563832646), pollutant = c("Ozone",

"NO2", "Ozone", "NOx", "Ozone", "PM25", "Ozone", "PM10", "Ozone",

"PM10")), .Names = c("seq", "group", "Outcome", "pinc", "lcinc",

"ucinc", "pollutant"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c("1",

"2", "3", "4", "17", "18", "19", "20", "21", "22"))

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Pair error bars by group and factor
parts:
Hi:

There are several ways you could go about this, but here's one attempt:

library(ggplot2)

# Create a factor to indicate output-pollutant combinations
cv2$set <- factor(rep(1:5, each = 2), labels = c("cardva-NO2", "cardva-NOx",
"ami-PM25", "ami-PM10", "ischem-PM10"))

ggplot(cv2, aes(x = factor(group), y = pinc, color = pollutant)) +
geom_point(size = 3) +
geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lcinc, ymax = ucinc), width = 0.3, size = 1) +
labs(x = "group") +
facet_wrap(~ set, nrow = 1)

I decided to plot by group since Ozone is always in group 1 and the comparison
is always in group 2. My initial thought was to dodge by pollutant,
but the problem is
that since Ozone is always group 1 that the two Ozone error bars
always overlap in
group 1. The above was a compromise to ensure that each pair was being
plotted separately.

An alternative would be to use pollutant for the x-variable and try to
dodge by group, but
you run into the same overlap problem: Ozone is always group 1. There
are probably
better ways to do this, but since you didn't indicate the type of plot
you wanted this is one
shot at it.

The reason why I generated the set variable was because each pair of
groups was neither
associated with a unique outcome variable nor a unique comparison pollutant. By
combining the two, I was able to generate unique pairs. This seemed
reasonable to me
because Ozone was present in every pair and it wasn't immediately
clear why you would
want to compare the Ozone results against each other.

Dennis

Thus I want to compare the effect of ozone with other pollutants on this single outcome. What I want is to have a plot with a legend of ozone and the other pair of pollutant on x-axis rather than by  group (1 and 2).
